professional: a senior battery-modelling / BMS engineer who does state-of-power and endurance estimation for UAV and EV packs (Thevenin equivalent-circuit models, HPPC voltage-limited power per the USABC/FreedomCAR battery test manual, Plett's SOP estimation); first checks: is the constant-power current root the right branch, is the voltage-limited power formula right, do the nondimensional units survive a change of R0, are the cell parameters sourced, and is the result new against the SOP literature. (Note: 'sag' here is battery terminal-voltage sag, not conductor sag.)

evidence.correctness: The model and seven of the eight result sections recompute; section 5 (cold cell) is wrong by a factor k. Reproduction: `cd research/sag-twin && PYTHONPATH=src python3 experiments/run.py > /tmp/claude-0/audit-sag/results.txt; diff` against experiments/results.txt: identical, 1.3 s. Independent physical-units simulation, no subject import (`python3 -I /tmp/claude-0/audit-sag/indep.py`: E0 4.2 V, Q 5 Ah, R0 20 mOhm, current from Newton on V*I = P, Euler in seconds): flat-EMF ratio at u0 = 0.6 is 0.8163 vs eta 0.8162 (README 0.816); droop+cutoff at u0 = 0.2 gives T = 15.079 units, s_cut 0.0857, ratio 0.8617 (results 15.079, 0.0857, 0.8616); max deliverable power at s = 0.2 by scanning terminal voltage >= cutoff is 0.2800 (results 0.280); burst-0.5 floor 0.5143 (results 0.5143). Monte Carlo predicted sd sigma/sqrt(sum i^2) recomputed with my own Newton current (`python3 -I /tmp/claude-0/audit-sag/fit.py`): 0.0190, 0.0095, 0.0048 (matches). Cold cell, same independent script, R = k R0 at fixed physical power: real/twin = 0.7146, 0.5712, 0.2975 at k = 1.5, 2, 3, but results.txt:51-53 and whitepaper.md:16 report 0.4764, 0.2856, 0.0992. Cause: run.py:53 compares endurance(k*u) (time in units of k R0 Q/E0, the cold cell's unit) with twin_endurance(base) (warm units) without the factor k. The table contradicts itself: section 2 gives real/twin 0.5712 at u0 = 0.4, section 5 gives 0.2856 at u0_eff = 0.40. The closed forms (eta, s_cut, max_power) are right by hand: v i = u0/4, low-current root, and the voltage-limited max power 4 vc (e - vc)/r is the HPPC discharge-power formula P = Vmin (OCV - Vmin)/R.

evidence.fitness: A researcher could reuse the closed forms as a teaching reference, but the result is not new. Nearest prior work: the USABC/FreedomCAR Battery Test Manual (INL, 2003) HPPC 'available power' P = Vmin (OCV - Vmin)/R, which is this project's max_power and burst floor exactly; Plett (2004), 'High-performance battery-pack power estimation using a dynamic cell model', IEEE TVT, state-of-power under voltage limits; Abdilla, Richards & Burrow (2015), 'Power and endurance modelling of battery-powered rotorcraft', IROS, which already puts an internal-resistance cell under a constant-power rotorcraft load to predict endurance; Traub (2011) J. Aircraft on battery endurance with Peukert. Only Plett 2015 and Chen & Rincon-Mora are cited. The eta(u) formula is the classical constant-power source with series resistance. The project is one micro-question in its own slug, not a programme step (research/CLAUDE.md, PROGRAMMES.md). Nothing is checked against a measured cell or datasheet.
evidence.domain: Method is a standard R-only Thevenin model with a linear OCV and linear R(s), constant-power load, hard cutoff; correctly solved on the low-current branch. A BMS engineer would depart on: (a) parameters invented (d = 0.25 linear droop is far from a Li-ion OCV with a plateau and knee; vc = 0.70 E0) and not swept, although they drive the headline stranded-charge and burst-floor numbers; (b) the 'twin' is an R = 0 straw man and the 'constant derate' a straw man, while practice (HPPC-based SOP) already uses R; (c) no RC polarisation branch, so burst-floor numbers ignore that short bursts see only the ohmic part of R (the paper lists this as a limit); (d) the cold-cell section mishandles the nondimensional time unit when R0 changes, the kind of error a practitioner would catch with a one-line units check; (e) R identification is in-family with the OCV known exactly, so 1-2% is a best case (section 8 partly addresses this).

defects.what: Cold-cell section reports real/twin endurance low by the factor k: run.py compares endurance(k*u0) in the cold cell's time unit (k R0 Q/E0) with twin_endurance(base) in the warm unit (R0 Q/E0). Reported 0.476, 0.286, 0.099, 0.012 at k = 1.5, 2, 3, 4; correct 0.715, 0.571, 0.298, 0.047 (identical to section 2's rows at u0 = 0.3, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, which the table itself contradicts). Published in whitepaper result 5.

Tests leave the droop path and the twin unpinned: changing D 0.25 -> 0.20, making the twin ignore droop, or replacing the twin's mean EMF with the full-charge EMF all leave 9/9 green, though each changes every section-2-to-8 headline. run.py (where the cold-cell bug lives) has no test.

Cell parameters d = 0.25 (linear OCV droop) and vc = 0.70 are invented and never swept, although they set every stranded-charge and burst-floor number; research/CLAUDE.md asks for sourced parameters or a sweep showing the conclusion survives.

Nearest prior work not cited and novelty not positioned: the burst-floor / max-power result is the USABC/FreedomCAR HPPC voltage-limited available-power formula P = Vmin (OCV - Vmin)/R; state-of-power estimation (Plett 2004, IEEE TVT) and constant-power rotorcraft endurance with internal resistance (Abdilla, Richards & Burrow 2015, IROS) already cover the endurance and burst questions.
s_cut divides by d + rho*k and raises ZeroDivisionError for a flat EMF (d = 0, rho = 0), e.g. endurance(0.3, d=0.0); should return 0 (no cutoff before empty) when num >= 0.
'Stranded' charge is charge left at the cutoff at that power; it is recoverable at lower power, so the word overstates the loss.
README says run.py takes about 10 s; it takes 1.3 s.

verdict: A small, clean, reproducible equivalent-circuit study: results.txt regenerates byte-identically in 1.3 s, the closed forms (eta(u) = (1+sqrt(1-u))/2, the cutoff state, the voltage-limited max power) are right, and five reported numbers recompute in an independent physical-units simulation. It misses the bar: the cold-cell section (whitepaper result 5) is wrong by a factor k because the nondimensional time unit changes with R0 (0.286 reported at k = 2 where the true ratio is 0.571, which the same table's section 2 already shows), half the seeded mutants in the twin and droop path survive the 9 tests, the driving parameters are invented and unswept, and the main burst-floor result is the standard HPPC available-power formula, uncited, so the research contribution is a textbook consequence of an R-only Thevenin model rather than a new result.
